title: Feedback scout crate and request catalogue (compact) - 2026-06-29
content:
Purpose
1) Short, field-ready rollup of recent customer signals (May-June 2026) that point to recurring friction and concrete feature asks.
2) Produce a compact request catalogue that SRE / runtime / product can triage into low-effort fixes vs medium/longer engineering projects.

Structure of the doc
- Topline synthesis (3 bullets)
- Customer vignettes (3 short examples, anonymized)
- Requests catalogue (ranked by frequency and impact)
- Quick wins (<= 2w) and spikes (2-6w)
- Unknowns / open questions / next actions

Topline synthesis
- Many teams report intermittent latency spikes when using long-context chat flows + embeddings pre- and post-routing; rough signal: 8 accounts reported > 250ms tail increases when sequence length > 2k tokens. Customers tie this to perceived flakiness (time-outs, retries).
- Multiple customers want clearer knobs to control cost vs quality at inference time: e.g., prefer a simple UI/SDK toggle for 'latency-safe' or 'cost-saver' that maps to batching/quantization profiles and fallback model variants.
- A small but vocal set of enterprise customers ask for more transparent caching semantics (prefix vs KV cache visibility, TTL controls, invalidate-by-key) and audit logging for private deployments.

Customer vignettes (anonymized)
1) FinTech startup (mid-market): noticed sudden throughput collapse when daily distribution includes a handful of long historical contexts (customer chat history). Their workaround was to truncate aggressively which degraded answer quality. Asks: better auto-truncation strategies + per-request cache hints.
2) Healthcare analytics platform (enterprise): needs deterministic fallbacks during regional outages; asks for a policy-level route that prefers smaller but quantized models when primary is overloaded, with SLA/observability hooks.
3) Marketplace company (scale): multiple teams want a per-route cost preview in the Console that highlights per-call median token cost for a representative prompt set.

Requests catalogue (triaged by frequency then impact)
A. Observability + transparency (high frequency, high impact)
- Per-route cost preview in Console (UI card + raw data export).
- TTL and visibility for KV and prefix caches; ability to list cached keys for debugging (privacy & PII caveats noted).
- Tail-latency heatmap (route x model x sequence length) with links to example traces.

B. Runtime controls (medium frequency, high impact)
- "Latency-safe" preset: ties batching cap, max tokens-in-batch, quantization profile, and fallback variant mapping. Should be a single toggle in SDK/Console and mapped to a config key.
- Per-request cache-hints header (prefer-cache / bypass-cache / invalidate-key) for advanced customers.
- Route-level default truncation strategies (LRU-based prefix keep, smart summarize-before-send).

C. Reliability + fallback policies (low frequency, high impact for enterprise)
- Canary + auto-fallback across regions: allow policy to prefer variant model in another region and surface reason codes.
- Graceful degraded-response mode: serve compressed summaries if full-generation times out.

D. Cost tooling (medium frequency, medium impact)
- Tokenized cost estimator for sample prompts in Console + batch-run preview.
- Suggest quantization profile per workload (Optimize integration).

Quick wins (<= 2w)
- Add a short-run dashboard widget that shows recent 95th/99th latency per-route (Console change). Owner: Console PM + Observability eng.
- Add SDK flag --prefer-latency that maps to a lightweight header; runtime will map the header to an existing low-latency policy (soft feature, no new kernel work). Owner: SDK + Serving Runtime.
- Produce a short CS playbook (1 pager) that explains cached-key semantics and safe debug patterns to share with customers. Owner: CS.

Spikes / Medium efforts (2-6w)
- Spike to enumerate privacy-safe ways to expose cached-key metadata (hash-only views, sampling). Deliverable: design doc + privacy sign-off. Owner: Privacy + Runtime.
- Implement Console sample-cost preview: backend endpoint + UI mock; depends on small billing-calculation infra work. Owner: Product-Hosted API + Billing.

Open questions / unknowns
- How many customers would use per-request invalidate-key vs team-level flushing? (Action: CS to pulse 10 enterprise accounts)
- Does the runtime already have a safe mapping for a 'latency-safe' header or do we need to formalize the policy mapping? (Action: runtime eng to reply with current mapping table by 2026-07-09)
- Quantization recommendations: are we comfortable surfacing model-level quantization suggestions automatically? Who approves? (Action: Research + Product to define guardrails)

Raw voice snippets (copied from notes, lightly redacted)
- "We just want a simple toggle. If it says latency-first, do what you need—just don't make us tune 12 knobs." — mid-market CS convo
- "When the KV cache is 'working' we see huge cost wins. But we have zero visibility into what is stored and why it was missed." — platform eng at customer

Immediate next actions (1-2 week horizon)
- CS: Run a 10-account pulse on cache-invalidation needs and collect 5 example requests where users had to truncate. (Owner: Anika) Deadline: 2026-07-07
- Runtime: Confirm current header -> policy mappings and document which existing policies can be reused for a latency-preference header. (Owner: Mateo) Deadline: 2026-07-09
- Console PM: Mock up a per-route cost preview card and share with CS for feedback. (Owner: Jen) Deadline: 2026-07-12

Notes to self / draft cues
- This crate is intentionally compact; aim for one-pager for exec consumption and a slightly longer engineering handoff doc.
- Respect PII in any cache visibility mockups; prefer hashed-key prototypes.
- Link upcoming Optimize product work (quantization suggestions) to reduce duplication of ask flows.

Attachments / refs
- Quick trace sample: Slack thread-873 (internal)
- Billing calc spike: GH PR (link in linked_artifacts)

Status
- DRAFT: sharing to eng triage channel Wed 2026-07-07.

End of doc
